text:
elaine: heads up — saw a spike in duplicate token billing this morning tied to clients reconnecting during the graceful-close window. seems like the new reconnect heuristic in canary is dropping the lease earlier than before :grimacing:
rajesh: ugh. any reproducible trace?
tobi: saw that too, caught a sample in staging. logs show lease release followed by immediate reconnect which creates a new session id. client resumes but billing replays.
elaine: paste of log snippet (sanitized):
```
[10:12:30Z] session=abc123 lease=held ttl=120
[10:12:55Z] session=abc123 lease=release reason=grace_timeout new_heuristic=true
[10:12:56Z] proxy=edge1 reconnect token=abc123 resumption=false billed=true
```
jamal: interesting — so the proxy releases the lease before the client has chance to resume. Are we clearing the resume token on lease release?
rajesh: yes current flow: lease->release clears opaque session and resume token to avoid orphaned state. the canary changed order (release then accept reconnect) to reduce stuck leases under heavy load.
elaine: the side effect is duplicate billing when the client retries in that tiny window. console shows two per-route requests and billing delta.
tobi: telemetry query I ran: `sum(count) by (route, event) where event in (connect, resume, bill)` shows a sharp >1.8x spike for a 45s period.
jamal: options: increase lease_grace_ms so release waits, or change release path to keep resume-token until reconnect accepted, or make reconnect idempotent at billing layer (dedupe by resume-id).
rajesh: keeping token longer worries me about stuck leases causing capacity pressure. but billing dedupe is messy for long tail.
elaine: UX-wise we should also show the affected sessions in the Console per-route panel (hover to see lease state + last action). People are triaging from alerts and can't see the handshake state.
tobi: +1 for Console change. quick mitigation: revert canary or tweak heuristic to hold 200ms. Can we instrument a metric for "lease_release_before_resume"?
ops-bot: canary-rollout: canary at 20% since 10:05Z; monitoring alert rule r=lease_release_retries firing 3m ago
jamal: ok immediate plan: revert to previous order on canary (release after accepting reconnect) for the <20% batch, add metric, and open a follow-up to design resume-idempotent billing.
rajesh: implementation note — reorder means proxy must accept reconnect on same path that holds the lease. requires a short path change in session manager: `try_resume -> extend_lease -> accept` instead of `extend_lease -> clear -> accept` (pseudo).
elaine: can we test in staging with flaky network to reproduce? qa-bot: scheduled job created: `flaky-reconnect-stress` against staging at 13:00Z (runs 30m) :white_check_mark:
jamal: timeline: revert canary now -> monitor consoles/dashboards for 30m -> if stable, replan proper fix (dedupe or controlled grace). ops-bot: rollback initiated for canary group at 10:28Z
rajesh: we'll also add a small dashboard tile: "recent lease-release-before-resume samples" and a link to the trace in the console. can someone own the follow-up ticket?
elaine: I'll file the ticket for resume-idempotent billing + Console trace UI. tagging @rajesh for design review. :thumbsup:
rajesh: added comments on the ticket draft. thanks everyone for quick triage.
elaine: leaving this thread open until the staging run ends, will post results.
